speaker: Doctor
text: I understand you've presented with seizures, lethargy, and other neurological signs three days after birth. To better understand your condition, I need to know if there was any maternal fever or infection during pregnancy or labor, and if you were exposed to any known toxins or medications during gestation.

speaker: Patient
text: 1100-g (2-lb 7-oz) newborn, 31 weeks' gestation. The patient was born three days ago with a birth weight of 1100 g at 31 weeks' gestation. The antenatal period was complicated by chorioamnionitis. Apgar scores were 3 and 6 at 1 and 5 minutes, respectively. The patient has become increasingly lethargic over the past 18 hours and experienced a tonic seizure lasting for 25 seconds.

speaker: Doctor
text: Given the history of chorioamnionitis, low birth weight, and early-onset seizures, I suspect a severe bacterial infection such as Group B Streptococcus or Gram-negative sepsis. REQUEST TEST: Blood culture, CBC with differential, and C-reactive protein (CRP). DIAGNOSIS READY: Early-onset Neonatal Sepsis likely caused by Group B Streptococcus.
